_comment: Risk-calibration golden vectors — the false-positive/false-negative corpus.
Two-sided contract: every 'benign' vector must score AT/BELOW its max_risk in
every layer it covers; every 'risky' vector must score AT/ABOVE its min_risk.
Bounds, not exact totals: intentional tuning may move scores inside the band;
drifting past a bound is a calibration regression and fails CI.
app/lib/guard/evidence.ts classifyAct (the server's act classifier, which grades
what will RUN rather than what was declared, and whose flags gate the
evidence-flag policies). The guard takes max(client, server, evidence),
so a false positive in ANY layer interrupts an agent.
TO ADD A CASE: when an interruption is judged wrong (or a dangerous action
scores low), add a vector here with source naming the incident, set the bound,
fix the model if warranted, and ship both in the same commit.
(client vectors — it filters on client_expected, so a server-only or
evidence-only vector is skipped there) — spec:

vectors.label: benign

vectors.name: rm-rf-regenerable-subtree
vectors.label: benign
vectors.source: 2026-08-11 calibration probe: 'rm -rf node_modules/.cache' graded 100/security while 'rm -rf node_modules' graded 35/cleanup. The bare-name allowlist made a strict subset outrank its own superset; deleting part of a regenerable root cannot be more dangerous than deleting all of it. Both mirrors now match subtrees (evidence.ts isRegenerableArtifactTarget, bash_classifier.py _is_regenerable_dir_name).

vectors.name: rm-rf-regenerable-subtree-traversal-escape
vectors.label: risky
vectors.source: 2026-08-11 two-sided companion to rm-rf-regenerable-subtree. Widening the allowlist to subtrees removed the implicit guarantee that a bare name cannot contain '..', so the traversal, absolute-path and home-path rejections became explicit. Pinned here so a future simplification cannot quietly drop them.

vectors.name: git-log-date-format-flag
vectors.label: benign
vectors.source: 2026-08-16 incident: 1,759 require_approval decisions in 7 days on read-only git log. The 2026-07-01 (?<!-) fix rejects --format= but NOT --date=format: (the preceding char is =), so every git-log command scored +20 destructive and hit the 100 clamp the org's threshold-100 rule gated on. Operator disabled every policy in the org. Modeled here as review/reversible/execution like its sibling git-show-format-flag: a read-only git log IS low risk. (Separately worth noting, NOT fixed here: the live hook classified these as action_type=apply, base 60, which is its own miscalibration.)

vectors.name: npm-run-format-script
vectors.label: benign
vectors.source: 2026-08-16 incident, same root cause: a formatter script name is not a disk format. Bare  format  scored +20 on every `npm run format` — SERVER-side only (DESTRUCTIVE_GOAL_PATTERNS), fixed in 146a9917, which is what server_expected pins. The client never had a format boost: `npm run format`, `npm run build` and `npm run lint` all score 30 identically, because that 30 is package_management's ordinary base and nothing to do with the word. The original client max_risk of 25 asserted a mechanism that does not exist on this side and was red from the day it landed. Whether `npm run <script>` deserves a lower base than `npm install` is a real open calibration question, but it is a separate decision from this incident.

vectors.name: format-drive-letter
vectors.label: risky
vectors.source: 2026-08-16 counter-vector: narrowing format to a device object must keep the Windows drive-letter form matching, not just the prose form pinned by format-disk-prose.

vectors.name: psql-select-benign
vectors.label: benign
vectors.source: RFC 2026-09-04-database-containment: the shell classifier's new `database` branch grades a client's inline SQL. A read-only SELECT through psql must stay in the review band — grading every psql call as a migration is exactly the alarm fatigue the branch is meant to avoid.

vectors.name: psql-inline-ddl
vectors.label: risky
vectors.source: RFC 2026-09-04-database-containment: before the branch, `psql -c "drop table users"` graded other/30 with NO flags — a mass-destructive database act was invisible to every evidence-gated policy. It must never carry protected_target (the default packs' mass-destructive line keys on that flag, 2026-08-21), so honest grading does not change a fresh install's hold behavior.

vectors.name: prisma-migrate-deploy
vectors.label: risky
vectors.source: RFC 2026-09-04-database-containment: a migration tool's statements live in files the server never sees, so it grades migrate/60 rather than by inline SQL. npx/pnpm/yarn/bunx prefixes are transparent to the command slot.

vectors.name: git-commit-message-mentioning-psql
vectors.label: benign
vectors.source: RFC 2026-09-04-database-containment, ordering counter-vector: a commit message describing the database branch is inert data git never executes. The database branch sits INSIDE classifyShellSegment, after the inert-git-message early return, so this stays git_message/35.
vectors.bash_command: git commit -m "grade psql -c drop table users as a database act"
